questions.q: What is the unit of pressure?

engage.hook: A sealed aerosol can left in a hot car can explode.

reveal.question: Why does the can fail?
reveal.answer: Heat speeds up the gas particles inside. They hit the walls harder and more often, and pressure builds until the can gives way.

learn.heading: Gas Behaviour

items: Pressure is caused by particle collisions with the walls

learn.imageDescription: diagram of gas particles in a container with arrows showing collisions with walls

learn.heading: Ideal Gas Law
learn.example: 2 mol of gas at 300 K in a 0.05 m³ container: p = (2 × 8.31 × 300) / 0.05 = 99 720 Pa

build.q: A gas is compressed at constant temperature. What happens to the pressure?
build.explanation: Boyle's Law: at constant T, p is proportional to 1/V — halving volume doubles pressure.

developing.q: State what pV = nRT is called.

mastering.q: Explain why the ideal gas law breaks down at very high pressures.
mastering.a: At high pressures, gas particles are close enough that intermolecular forces and particle volume become significant.
